How does Nuvexa identify the correct customer, delivery address and customer-specific product numbers?

From several signals at once: sender details, subject line, letterhead, customer number, order history and your existing identification rules. Delivery addresses and customer-specific product numbers are checked against your master data, and ambiguous cases are flagged, never guessed.
What happens if Nuvexa is not certain about a line item?

It goes to your team for review instead of straight into the ERP. Every line item is marked as confident, uncertain or unresolved, and you can increase automation step by step once results have proven stable on your real orders.
How much of the order process can run automatically?

As much as your data allows, and you decide how much. A automation rate depends on your document quality and product range, so we measure it on your actual orders instead of quoting a generic percentage. You set which cases run fully automatically and at what confidence threshold.
How are orders created in the ERP, and how are price, delivery date and availability handled?

Nuvexa structures the incoming order and transfers it into your ERP. Where supported, the order is simulated first: price differences, requested delivery dates, availability issues, blocked products and other ERP feedback show up directly in Nuvexa for review. Pricing itself stays in your ERP.
Is our order data shared with other customers or competitors?

No. Each customer works in a separate tenant environment. Your orders, customer data, corrections and learned rules are never shared with other customers, including competitors, and this is contractually guaranteed.
How quickly can we get started?

Usually within two working days. Nuvexa runs a technical test on your product master data and real orders from your inbox. Your team checks the results first; the ERP integration only follows once the process has proven itself.
How much implementation effort is required on our side?
Very little at the start: provide the relevant data and give your team time to test. Your IT only gets involved once you decide to move from testing to integration.

How accurately does the AI match our products?

Accuracy depends on your catalog and your requests, so we don’t rely on a generic benchmark. Instead, we test Nuvexa on your own bills of quantities, and you see within days how accurately it performs in your environment.
How long do we need to train the system beforehand?
No upfront training is needed. Nuvexa starts with your existing product data, descriptions and past quotes, and improves with every confirmation and correction from your team.
What does Nuvexa learn from, and who do corrections apply to?
Only from your own team. Confirmations and corrections take effect immediately in the bill of quantities you’re working on and apply to all future requests.
What data does Nuvexa need, and what happens if our product data is incomplete?

Your product master data with short and long descriptions, plus a handful of real bills of quantities. Incomplete data is no problem: you don’t need a fully maintained PIM, because Nuvexa also reads datasheets, technical documentation and catalog text.
How does Nuvexa integrate with our ERP, and where does pricing happen?

Nuvexa sends matched products, quantities and units straight to your ERP via API, Updates or other formats. Pricing and calculation stay in your existing system, so your commercial logic remains untouched.
Is our data shared with other customers or competitors?
No. Each customer works in a separate tenant environment. Your data, corrections and learned rules are never shared with other customers, including competitors, and this is contractually guaranteed.
How quickly can we get started?
Usually within two working days. A technical test with your own product data and real requests shows results before any ERP integration is needed, so IT effort stays low at the start.

Every business has its own goals. Nuvexa helps your team plan the next step and keep things moving.

A simpler way to work together

Nuvexa reads tenders and BoQs in any format for your project team, requests supplier prices for items you don’t stock, and books emailed orders into your ERP for your order desk. No retyping, no copying between Outlook and notes.
Built for technical distributors with complex assortments, high request volumes and an existing ERP landscape. ISO/IEC 27001 certified.
"What used to take two days now takes two hours."
Up from roughly 70% at Customer A, including unstructured requests.
Across our customers, faster quotes turn into more won business.
More figures and details in the customer stories →
Your project team loses days reading tenders and chasing supplier prices. Your order desk retypes every emailed order. Projects get declined, and orders wait.
A 48-page BoQ takes 1.5 days just to read, so you bid on only a fraction of the projects you’re invited to.
Every supplier request is an email written by hand, and every reply is a price retyped from Outlook or OneNote.
Installers email orders and call-offs as PDFs, and every line is keyed into the ERP by hand.
Nuvexa reads any tender, not just Updates. It matches every line item to your range, checks it against the spec and sends the result to your ERP and to every customer.

Updates file, PDF, scan or plain email: Nuvexa reads them all and turns even long tenders into structured line items with quantities and long texts. Your project team bids on every project, not only the ones it has time to read.
A same tender often goes out to 6–10 customers. Nuvexa sends it to your ERP and exports it as Updates and PDF for each one, long texts included, so your team no longer reformats every file by hand.
Supplier requests for your Project team

Nuvexa turns the positions of the LV you’re quoting into price requests to the right manufacturers, and reads their replies back into your quote. Your supplier prices stay in the same flow as the tender — not in Outlook and OneNote.
Pick the line items you don’t stock, and Nuvexa creates the price requests. No more copying items into one email per supplier.
Supplier profiles group line items by supplier automatically, so no request is missed and none goes out twice.
Upload a supplier’s reply and Nuvexa matches the prices to your line items. Special prices stay in the quote, not in Outlook or OneNote.
Supplier RFQ for your Project team

Nuvexa turns the line items you don’t stock into price requests to the right suppliers and reads their replies back into your quote. Supplier prices stay in the same flow as the tender, not in Outlook and OneNote.
Order entry for your order desk

Nuvexa turns the orders already arriving by email into ERP orders and learns your range and your customers’ wording as it goes. So you automate the orders your web shop never gets, without asking installers to change how they order.
Orders, call-offs, inquiries and complaints share one inbox. Nuvexa recognizes the orders, including those forwarded from branches, and routes each one to the right person on your order desk.
Installers order in their own words, with old or manufacturer article numbers. Nuvexa learns each customer’s wording and maps it to your article master. A lookup happens once, not on every order.
Approved orders go into your ERP as real sales orders, with header, lines and quantities. Your order desk gets time back for customers, advice and follow-ups instead of typing.

Three customers, three measured outcomes — and the story behind each one.
We configure Nuvexa for your products and rules, connect the relevant data sources, and validate the business case with a selected user group on historical and live requests.
Selected users work with Nuvexa in their day-to-day process. Feedback and real decisions continuously improve the setup for your specific way of working.
With the workflow established, Nuvexa can be extended to additional teams, entities and countries without starting again from scratch.

Industrial master data was never built for AI. Nuvexa is designed for historic article numbers, customer-specific descriptions, abbreviations, missing fields, unusual units, and hundreds of thousands of SKUs.
Typos, abbreviations, free text, and inconsistent terminology are recognized for what customers actually mean.
Nuvexa connects to your current catalog and systems without requiring a data-cleansing project first.
Preferred products, equivalents, and in-house matching rules become part of the workflow—not a spreadsheet next to it.
Low-confidence results are presented for review; the release decision stays with the sales representative.
Nuvexa sits between customer requests, product data, and your ERP, without asking teams to replace the systems they rely on today.
Connect via APIs, webhooks, a secure gateway, or files—whatever your landscape supports today.
Single sign-on, two-factor authentication, role-based permissions, and a complete audit trail.
Your workspace remains the system of record; Nuvexa delivers structured data into the process.
First workflows go live in weeks, not quarters—planned together with your IT.
